publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Depth image-based rendering (DIBR), which is used to render virtual views with a color image and the corresponding depth map, is one of the key techniques in the 2D to 3D conversion process. One of the main problems in DIBR is how to reduce holes that occur on the generated virtual view images. In this paper, a region-wise rendering framework, which divides the original image regions into three special classes and renders each with optimal adaptive process respectively, is introduced. With the optimized region-wise processing, kinds of existing DIBR methods can be combined together to achieve better visual rendering results. Numerical experimental results demonstrate the good performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dynamic information extraction for the big data
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: For the practical big time series data, it is the important step to eliminate the noise and get the dynamic information of the time series data. For the series data, the extraction model and the transform model are given in this paper, and the sampling interval of the models is discussed to guarantee the estimated system convergence. The dynamic information is analyzed according to the estimated dynamic characteristic. The experiment results show that for the time series data, the dynamic information extracted by Kalman filter is feasible, and can be used to analyze the trend characteristic effectively.

articleTitle: Real-time vehicle counting method based on image sequences with laser line
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Being robust to changeable illumination and shadow are essential requirements of a practical vehicle counting system. In this paper, we come up with a method that detects vehicle by analyzing the state of laser line projected on lane. In addition, we use the entropy of histogram of oriented gradients (HOG) descriptor extracted from the region of interest (ROI) to quantify area percent of vehicle in a ROI. Normalized HOG descriptor is with better invariance to illumination and shadow, which makes a great contribution to the robustness of our method. Once the laser line disappears or appears in an image, we use entropy of HOG to judge that whether a vehicle is driving into or driving out of the ROI. We tested this method under different conditions, experimental results also prove that our method is robust to the change of illumination, and shadow of vehicles has no impact on accuracy and recall rate of detection result.

articleTitle: Vibration suppression of an axially moving system by adaptive boundary control
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive boundary control for vibration suppression of an axially moving belt system with high acceleration/deceleration under unknown distributed disturbance is developed by using Lyapunov's synthesis method and adaptive technique. The infinite dimensional model of the belt system is derived by utilizing the extended Hamilton's principle. The adaptive law and sign function are employed to compensate for the system parametric uncertainties and deal with unknown boundary disturbance. The S-curve acceleration/deceleration method is adopted to plan the speed of the belt. With the proposed control scheme, the stability of the closed-loop system is ensured, and the performance of the designed control scheme has been successfully demonstrated through simulations.

articleTitle: Caption detection and removal from video images with complicated background using intelligent inpainting scheme
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Effectively finding and removing the captions embedded in video images and restoring the covered background have great significance on video reuse. In this paper, considering the captions color and edge features, we first present a method of caption extraction based on the color edge detector and connected domain features analysis, which can reduce the false detection rate when the gray scale of text is close to background. Meanwhile, the proposed algorithm has stronger robustness and adaptability for captions of different types and countries. Next, after caption detection, we improve a method based on Criminisi algorithm for repairing the text in video image with complex background. We put forward three improvements about this algorithm. First, the fixed size of the template blocks will be changed into the variable ones. Second, we use addition instead of multiplication in computing the priority of repairing blocks. Third, we combine the Euclidean distance between the blocks with the sum of squared differences (SSD) matching criterion. Experimental results demonstrate that our method leads to good results in both detecting the captions and maintaining the video image texture and structure information at the same time.

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis for a hydraulic servo system using wavelet packet and neural network
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Hydraulic servo system is widely used in the project, and it's crucial for the reliability of hydraulic system. Due to the nonlinear, time-varying and noise in the hydraulic system, the traditional fault diagnosis methods have been unable to meet the requirements. To decrease false alarm rate of hydraulic servo system, an adaptive fault detection method based on RBF observer and an adaptive threshold is presented. First, an RBF observer is established to obtain the residual by subtracting actual output from the estimated output by observer. Second, input command signal and output displacement signal of hydraulic servo system were decomposed into different wavelet frequency band which was input RBF neural network to get time-frequency adaptive threshold. Third, fault is detected by comparing the residual with adaptive threshold. Lastly, experimental results demonstrated that the proposed method is effective in detecting fault of hydraulic servo system.

articleTitle: Hysteresis model identification of piezoelectric ceramic actuators
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Piezoelectric ceramic actuators have wide application prospects in precision positioning and measurement technology, but its hysteresis characteristics cause a lot of restrictions to their applications. To solve this problem, in this paper, the hysteresis characteristic of piezoelectric ceramics is analyzed, and the data of the experiment are collected, the piezoelectric ceramic hysteresis curves at different excitation signal are analyzed and studied, and the fitting curve is got based on the experimental data. In order to establish hysteresis model of piezoelectric ceramic actuators, the curve fitting toolbox of MATLAB is used. The experiment results show that the model built can accurately describe hysteresis nonlinearity of the piezoelectric actuators.

articleTitle: Path finding for a NAO humanoid robot by fusing visual and proximity sensors
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Humanoid robot path finding is one of the core-technologies in robot research domain. This paper presents an approach to finding a path for robot motion by fusing images taken by the NAO's camera and proximity information delivered by sonar sensors. The NAO robot takes an image around its surroundings, uses the fuzzy color extractor to segment its potential path colors, and selects a fitting line as path by the least squares method. Therefore, the NAO robot is able to perform the automatic navigation according to the selected path. As a result, the experiments are conducted to navigate the NAO robot to walk to a given destination and to grasp a box. In addition, the NAO robot uses its sonar sensors to detect a barrier and helps pick up the box with its hands.

articleTitle: Iterative learning control of a minimal half-center oscillator
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Half-center oscillator is one form of central pattern generators, which could generate rhythmic motor patterns. In this paper, we create a minimal half-center oscillator composed of two Izhikevich models connected via chemical inhibitory synapses, and use closed-loop iterative learning control algorithm to regularize the bursting firing activity of the half-center oscillator through adapting one of maximal synaptic conductance. Simulation results show that closed-loop iterative learning control not only can rapidly find the best coupling strength that leads to the regularization goal but also change the coupling strength automatically according to different control precisions.

articleTitle: Filtering based multi-innovation stochastic gradient identification algorithm for multivariable nonlinear equation-error autoregressive systems
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper considers the parameter estimation problem of the multivariable Hammerstein systems with colored noise. By means of the adaptive filtering technique, a new adaptive filtering configuration consisting of a noise whitening filter and a recursive algorithm is developed. Then an adaptive filtering based multi-innovation stochastic gradient (F-MISG) identification algorithm is presented. The simulation results show that the proposed F-MISG algorithm has a higher parameter estimation accuracy and a faster convergence rate than the multi-innovation stochastic gradient algorithm for the same innovation length.

articleTitle: Determination of optimal process parameters to prepare licorice extract micro-particles using artificial neural network based particle swarm optimization
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The ways to obtain high-quality licorice extract (LE) micro-particles have a large impact on their aqueous solubility and bioavailability. Researchers have addressed their preparation and property modification problems. A new issue arises when decision-makers want to determine automatically the best process parameters to prepare them to minimize mean particle size. To do so, this work presents an intelligent decision-making method to obtain the optimal process parameters to prepare them. By using already obtained experimental data, we apply a hybrid algorithm integrating artificial neural network and particle swarm optimization to obtain the best experimental conditions for preparing LE micro-particles. The results indicate that this method is feasible and effective to determine the best process parameters.

articleTitle: Simultaneous calibration and mapping for mobile robot with non-holonomic constraint
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, a simultaneous calibration and mapping algorithm for mobile robot is proposed. The concept of expectation maximization (EM) are applied. Two main processes, mapping and calibration, are executed iteratively until converged. Graph SLAM are applied in mapping. For calibration, an innovative algorithm is proposed to decouple the whole problem into several sub-steps. And non-holonomic constraint of the mobile robot kinematics is utilized to speed up the computation. Experiment on an Autonomous Guided Vehicle (AGV) system are conducted to validate our algorithm.

articleTitle: Operator-based fault tolerant control for uncertain nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, operator based fault tolerant control for uncertain nonlinear system with actuator fault is considered by using operator based robust right coprime factorization approach. In detail, on the basis of the operator based control design structure, fault detection system design and fault tolerant control system design are considered for nonlinear system without and with uncertainty, respectively. In both of the proposed control system design, the fault signal can be detected and some sufficient conditions are given, which ensure that the designed system is stable and the output tracking performance can be realized. Finally, the theoretical analysis is applied onto an aluminium plate temperature control process and the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis is demonstrated by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Operator-based robust non-linear control for a two-link robot arm
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, a robust non-linear control scheme is proposed for a manipulator system by using the operator-based robust right coprime factorization approach. First the nonlinear feedback control scheme is proposed to eliminate effect of the uncertain plant. Second, robust stability of the present control system is discussed, and performance of output tracking is realized. Finally, effectiveness of the proposed method is confirmed by simulation results.

articleTitle: Optimization on RFID-enabled CONWIP control strategy for multi-echelon inventory of supply chain
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: It is very significant to study on the control strategies to improve the performance of multi-echelon inventory systems. As the ability of Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) that can count and locate products precisely, it provides a technical way to realize RFID-Enable electronic Card system, based on the system, the CONWIP strategy is extended to the multi-echelon inventory of supply chain. In this paper, a four-echelon inventory of supply chain is exemplified and the strategy is optimized by the simulation-based harmony search optimization method. The parameters of the strategy after optimization are made as the input to the simulation model. To verify the performance of the CONWIP strategy, it is compared with RFID-Enable (s, S) and Push strategies by simulation, the simulation results demonstrate that the strategy can reduce the total cost and enhance the service level effectively.

articleTitle: Sigmoid function array based ZG control for bounded input, energy saving and output tracking of time-invariant linear system
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The Zhang-gradient (ZG) method has been proved to be powerful for control problems solving. In view of the boundedness and safety of practical actuators through limiting the input, the sigmoid function array (SFA) based ZG (SFABZG) controller, designed by the combination of the SFA and the ZG method, is proposed and investigated for output tracking of the time-invariant linear (TIL) system in this paper. Simulation results substantiate the efficacy and superiority of the proposed novel controller for output tracking of the TIL system with the input bounded and energy saved.

articleTitle: A framework for context-aware semantic complex event processing
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: With the continuing increase in the heterogeneity and quantity of data source, such as data from sensors, social networks, business, usage of background knowledge and context information is a growing challenge in complex event processing. To remedy this problem, this paper proposes a framework for context-aware semantic complex event processing, in which domain ontology is used to annotate heterogeneous data and infer high-level context afterwards with declarative rules in the domain ontology and some application-specific rules, and event ontology is used to model events and analyze user query based on the definitions and relationships between events in it. In the process of complex event processing, context is taken into consideration to improve detection accuracy, meanwhile event correlation is made according to relations among events to forecast what will happen based on the detected events and current context information. User therefore can obtain timely and personalized results, i.e. user can get better understanding of current environment and make more correct decision. In this framework, semantic background knowledge is used to improve the expressiveness and flexibility of complex event processing systems. As a result, this framework can enable more intelligent event processing which can understand the semantics of events in a certain context.

articleTitle: Synchronization of pinning networks with Markovian switching topologies and event-triggered communication
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: We consider a continuous time Markovian switching dynamical network with time-varying connectivity and in which control of pinned nodes is event-triggered to reduce the frequency of controller updates and inter-node communication. We derive a sufficient condition relating the network graph Laplacian, the Markovian infinitesimal generator matrix governing the network switching, and the pinning control inputs to achieve exponential synchronization of the pinning network in the mean square sense. We provide a numerical example to illustrate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: LMI solution for local nonquadratic H∞ filter design of continuous-time T-S fuzzy systems
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the nonquadratic H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> filter design problem for continuous-time Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy systems. Attention is focused on the design of a stable filter guaranteeing a prescribed noise attenuation level in the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> sense. In order to derive less conservative results, conditions for designing H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> filter are established based on a relaxed approach in which both Finsler's Lemma and nonquadratic Lyapunov function are used. The well known problem of handing time-derivatives of membership functions (MFs) is overcomed by reducing global goals to the estimation of region of attraction. It is shown that conditions for the solvability of the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> filter design are written in the form of linear matrix inequality (LMI) which can be efficiently solved by convex optimization techniques. Simulation example is given to demonstrate the validity of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: An ACE-based method for evaluating the impact of DC interconnecting or AC tie line fault
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In an interconnection, frequency error and interchange power errors on tie lines are two sorts of important indices reflecting the control performance. However, these two indices may be impacted when a DC transmission line is put into operation, or an AC tie line fault occurs. In this paper, a method for evaluating the impacts is proposed, based on the theory of Area Control Error (ACE). First, the impact in the worst situation is figured. Then, we propose a model for simulating the ACE in the case when a DC tie line is put into operation, or an AC tie line fault occurs, using which we can evaluate the long-term effect. Finally, a numerical simulation is done. Compared with the real data, it shows that the method has a good performance for evaluating the impact of DC interconnecting or AC tie line fault.

articleTitle: Estimation for globally exponentially attractive set of a hyperchaotic Lorenz-type systems and its application
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The ultimate boundedness of a chaotic system is very important for the study of the qualitative behavior of a chaotic system. At present, explicit ultimate bound sets can be analytically obtained only for some special chaotic systems, and few results are known for hyperchaotic ones. In this paper, we investigate the ultimate boundedness for the new hyperchaotic Lorenz system by mathematical proof, and derive estimation of globally exponentially attractive set and positively invariant set. Using the estimation of the ultimate boundedness, we design a simple feedback controller to globally exponentially synchronize two hyperchaotic Lorenz systems, and present the results of numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Estimating fetal brain motion with total-variation-based magnetic resonance image registration
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Fetal magnetic resonance imaging has been widely used for brain malformation assessment, brain growth estimation and related disease diagnosis. However, how to estimate fetal brain motion is pending which hampers image interpretation. This paper presents an image registration method to address this problem. It takes total-variation regularization (TV) to model fetal brain motions and adopts a penalty toward piece-wise convergence. Based on four clinical cases, the proposed method was verified from perceived visual perception and landmark errors, and also compared to nonlinear Levenberg-Marquart least square optimization (L2). Visual perception indicates that TV-based registration outperforms L2-based method with less tissue difference, and landmark errors show that the landmark displacement decreases from 4.86±1.76mm to 0.82±0.51mm with L2-based method and to 0.42±0.57mm with TV-based method. One-way ANOVA verifies that both L2- and TV-based methods significantly reduce landmark errors (p<;0.0001), while TV-based method outperforms L2-based method (p<;0.0065). This paper provides a feasible solution to estimate fetal brain motions and benefits brain development study and disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Quadcopter autonomous control system based on image recognition
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Quadcopter has been widely used nowadays, but its autonomous flight capability is limited, some of the actions are carried out by human with remote control. When the communication channel is interfered, quadcopter cannot fly autonomously. In this paper, the image recognition technology is introduced into the traditional quadcopter which has the interface to add more functions. The control system is proposed and designed in this work, and the key technologies during realization are also discussed. The quadcopter can improve its ability of adjustment when the environment changes.

articleTitle: Predictive control based target tracking control for a carangiform robotic fish
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel target-tracking control scheme based on model predictive control for a faithful dynamics model of a carangiform robotic fish, aiming to solve the robust control problem of such under-actuated systems with control input constraints. We first discretize the dynamics model of the robot by transforming the nonlinear state-space representation into the linear time-varying representation. And a cost function is constructed to guarantee the target-tracking and satisfy the constrain on control input at the same time. Then the algorithm is given to calculate the optimized control input of the robotic in finite horizon during tracking a target. Finally, the effectiveness of the control scheme is demonstrated through simulation, and the effects of controller's parameters are analyzed and their selections are discussed further.

articleTitle: Operator-based control scheme for nonlinear feedback system
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The operator-based right coprime factorization method is applied to deal with the design and control issues for the nonlinear feedback systems. In details, the general case of the unimodular operator M is discussed since the satisfaction of the Bezout identity AN + BD = M is necessary and important in the method of right coprime factorization, where a sufficient condition is proposed by which the Bezout identity can be satisfied, which means that the stability of the nonlinear systems is guaranteed. A simulation of temperature control in the Peltier actuated thermal process is given to show the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Direct parametric control-oriented model transformations for a hypersonic vehicle
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Parametric control systems design approaches possess the advantage of providing all the degree of freedom in the system design and are very effective in dealing with multiple objective design. To facilitate the parametric control design for hypersonic vehicles (HVs), this paper derive the parametric control-oriented models for a general nonlinear longitudinal dynamical model of HVs. The force and moment coefficients in the original model are assumed to have some generalized forms. Both first-order quasi-linear model and matrix second-order nonlinear model have been developed without involving linearization in certain operating points, and the obtained results allow for direct application of parametric control design approach.

articleTitle: Control design of nonlinear networked systems under data packet dropouts
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In the paper, the research task of fuzzy control design is further investigated for one spec of nonlinear networked systems whose communication channels are unreliable. On account of previous results given by recent literature, a novel kind of fuzzy control law in case of that the variation information among arbitrarily many multi-instant normalized fuzzy weighting functions is proposed in order to conceive less conservative stabilization result. Owing to the underlying technical measure, relaxed result can be obtained by means of a set of linear matrix inequalities(LMIs). In the end, some simulation results are employed to illustrate the superiority of the proposed result.

articleTitle: A nonlinear auto-regressive Volterra model based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: As for nervous diseases study, building specific models tends to be really hard but significant. This paper introduces a novel method for neuron system identification using nonlinear auto-regressive Volterra (NARV) model based on the field programmable gate arrays (FPGA). We select HH model as a “black-box” system requiring identification, and obtain input and output data. A NARV model built on the FPGA implementation generates “the calculation output” instead of the known model. The NARV model is free-model and data-drive, requiring no accurate structure model but several series input and output data. This method is capable of the nonlinearities and uncertainties of nervous system. Combining with hardware technique makes it seem to be promising in the future.

articleTitle: Robust speech recognition based on speech enhancement and improved perceptual non-uniform spectral compression
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Owing to the decline of recognition rate of speech recognition system in noisy environments. In signal space, the speech enhancement algorithm which combines the Priori Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) with Auditory Masking Effect can effectively remove the noise of the speech signal. In feature space, improved non-uniform spectral perceptual compression feature extraction algorithm can effectively compress the speech signals in noisy environments and make the training and recognition environments more watchable. Finally, recognition rate can be greatly improved by the combination of two both. By experimenting on the intelligent medical bed platform, the result shows that the algorithm can effectively enhance the robustness of speech recognition, and ensure the recognition rate in noisy environments.

articleTitle: Trajectory tracking control of humanoid elbow joint based on neural network
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, the dynamic model of a kind of 2-DOF parallel mechanism driven by linear motor is established by Lagrange formulation combined with the dynamics characteristic of the linear motor. According to the uncertainty and nonlinearity of the system, a sliding mode control method of adaptive learning of upper bound based on RBF network is proposed. Using this control algorithm, the outputs of the system can track the desired trajectories. The method is proved to be effective based on the Lyapunov stability theory and simulation results.

articleTitle: Input-output finite-time stability and stabilization of stochastic fuzzy systems with randomly occurring uncertainties and gain fluctuations
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper studies the input-output finite-time stabilization problem of a class of fuzzy stochastic systems with randomly occurring uncertainties and (x, u)-dependent noises. By considering the randomly occurring gain fluctuations in controller gains, a fuzzy controller is designed to render the closed-loop system input-output finite-time stochastic stability with respect to some specified parameters. Through intensive stochastic analysis, a sufficient condition is established for the controller design via a convex optimization approach. A numerical example is exploited to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed design method.

articleTitle: The research and comparison on the combination technology of models based on HLA simulation
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In the HLA simulation system, there exist two kinds of model combination technology: the federation member level and the model level. In this paper, two kinds of model combination technology are introduced in detail, and through the comparison their advantages and disadvantages are analyzed. It shows that the combination on the member level is more applicable for the small simulation system, and the combination on the model level is more applicable for the medium and large simulation system.

articleTitle: Robust attack position of multi-UCAV based on ant colony algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The problem of generating a robust attack position plan for multi-UCAV cooperative attacking the moving target on the sea area is studied. There are many kinds of uncertain factors in the execution of multi-UCAV cooperative attack task, and the hostile target's maneuverability plays an important role. In order to handle the uncertainties in the cooperative attack mission well, a new approach based on the ant colony algorithm is proposed. Some constraints, such as the maneuverability constraints of UCAVs and the threat avoidance constraints, are considered to keep close to the reality of battlefield environment. And the robustness index of multi-UCAV cooperative attack position, which take into account the degree of uncertainty about the maneuvering target on the sea, is proposed to measure the robustness of UCAVs' attack position. According to the robustness index of multi-UCAV cooperative attack position, the solving approach for multi-UCAV cooperative attack position planning based on the ant colony algorithm is proposed to strengthen the robustness of UCAVs' attack position. The simulation experiment is provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the solving approach, and the simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is feasible for generating a strong robust attack position for UCAVs with both wide applicability and high efficiency.

articleTitle: An accurate and robust adaptive motion shadow detection algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to improve the results of shadow detection and remedy the defect that fixed threshold detection methods are difficult to adapt to different lighting environment, and to improve the detection and tracking accuracy of moving target, we propose an accurate, robust and adaptive motion shadow detection algorithm. The algorithm takes an advantage of the inner relationship between pixels pair and pixels. Firstly, the algorithm detects the first shadow candidate region by using the local color constancy (LCC) feature, and gets the region's largest connected domain with region growing method, and estimates the c1c2c3 detection thresholds based on the parameter estimation theory. In addition, we update the detection threshold in combination with an updating weight, so that it can automatically adapt to all kinds of ambient lighting environment. With the experiments on standard test set in different lighting conditions, we get the results that the proposed algorithm can effectively improve the results of sampling parameters estimation, besides, it has good robustness and improved detection accuracy compared with other methods, and the comprehensive evaluation index has reached above 94%.

articleTitle: Design of multi-parameter embedded biological information measurement system
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to overcome the disadvantages of poor portability and insufficient multifunctionality in traditional human health parameter measurement, a portable multi-parameter embedded electroencephalogram (EEG), electrocardiogram (ECG), and bioelectrical impedance (BEI) measuring system based on chip BMD101, the TGAM module, chip AD5933, STM32, and wireless Bluetooth transmission was designed and implemented in order to meet the requirements of accurate measurement. Experimental results show that the system has effective stability for continuous operation, and in contrast to professional instruments, the maximum deviation of electrical impedance measurement is not more than 2%, the deviation of the average heart rate can be confine within a range of ± 2, Therefore, the system has promising prospects for household applications.

articleTitle: An incentive-based supplier selection mechanism to support green supply chains
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Supplier selection is an important decision for an enterprise to realize a sustainable production. However, almost all works, which concerned the environmental issues, focused on the supplier selection or evaluation methods, rather than the incentive mechanism urging the participants to improve their decisions (reduce the harm to the environment). In this paper, not only are the commercial factors (price, quantity, and lead time), but also the environment factors (green factors and carbon dioxide emissions) of the suppliers are considered during the selection. The determinations of the green factors and the total carbon dioxide emissions depend on the analysis of the history trade data. An incentive supplier selection mechanism, which urges the agents to improve their decisions to reduce the harm to the environment, is proposed. Numerical calculations are provided to verify the feasibility and the superiority of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Performance assessment for aileron actuators based on MF-DFA and SOM neural network
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: To improve the robustness of performance assessment for aileron actuators, a novel performance assessment for aileron actuators using multi-fractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MF-DFA) and self-organizing mapping (SOM) neural network is first proposed. First, a generalized regression neural network (GRNN) is employed to establish a fault observer, then the residue is generated by subtracting the actual actuator system output from the observer output. Second, the residue's feature is extracted by MF-DFA. Third, SOM neural network, trained only by the normal residue's feature, is used to obtain the minimum quantization error (MQE) between the current feature and the normal feature, and the health confidence value (CV) is obtained by normalizing MQE. Lastly, four types of faults, namely electronic amplifier gain abrupt change, electronic amplifier gain gradual change, sensor gain change and cylinder leakage, are applied to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A grid method for robot path recognition based on RFID technology
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, a path planning of grid method based on RFID technology is presented. In the traditional sense, the grid method adopts the random searching, and uses the continuous subdivision of the grid to obtain the optimal path, so it would increase the difficulty of the path planning. Here, the grid method based on RFID technology is applied to achieve the optimal path planning globally via RFID and computer information interaction. Simulation experiment results demonstrate that the method can be used to effectively solve the problem of obstacle avoidance and path identification for intelligent robots patrolling.

articleTitle: High-performance three-phase high-power three-level rectifier using DSP-based digital control technique
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper focuses on the digital control technique and its industrialization of high-power three-phase three-level rectifier system. Firstly, the mathematical model of three-phase three-level VIENNA rectifier is established. The multiloop control method is realized based on the DQ coordinates, and a simplified three-level space vector pulse width modulation method which could simplify the calculation is proposed for the VIENNA rectifier. A composite control method of PI control and improved synchronous-frame repetitive control strategy is proposed to improve the quality of input current waveform. In order to improve the dynamic response of DC-bus, a power forward control strategy is proposed for the whole system. The whole system keeps unit power factor and pure sine input current. The modulation and control method of three-phase three-level rectifier is implemented in one DSP(digital signal processor). Experimental results of the 200kVA rectifier system show that the proposed modulation and control method is correct and effective.

articleTitle: Color binary correlation descriptor for image retrieval
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel image descriptor, called Color Binary Correlation (CBC), is proposed for image retrieval. This method defines and describes the structure elements utilizing binary patterns based on colors and edge orientation respectively, and thus integrate texture with the other two properties. Besides, its variants CBC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ri</sup> and CBC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u2</sup>, which are presented for rotated invariance and “unform” patterns respectively, are presented and analyzed for image retrieval. The experimental results in Corel-1K and Corel-10K datasets demonstrate that our descriptors are more robust and discriminative than other methods and CBC shows better performance than CBC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ri</sup> and CBC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u2</sup> because of taking more possible patterns into consideration.

articleTitle: Minimum interfering power based on interference matrix reconstruction for IA
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Interference alignment (IA) is a promising interference management technique to efficiently improve the degrees of freedom and system capacity in a K-user interference network. The existence of the interference channel (IC) is the main reason why communication system is interference limited. However, in most cases, transmission performance of interference sub-channels has remarkable differences. Existing IA schemes ignore the information of IC, resulting in limiting the performance of IA. Thus, this paper proposes an improved scheme, that is, minimum interfering power based on interference matrix reconstruction for IA. We firstly choose the influential sub-channels via comparing the interfering singular value with a predefined threshold, and then we target the interfering power minimization to achieve the IA solution. As the interfering power can be expressed as the trace of interfering matrix and we have known the Frobenius norm is less than or equal to the nuclear norm, we change the optimization function above into a nuclear norm optimization problem. Compared with existing schemes, the novel approach takes the influential interfering sub-channels into consideration, which makes the optimization process more pertinent and further eliminates interference at each receiver. Besides, proposed scheme can achieve the global optimal solution by utilizing nuclear norm optimization. Simulation results show the proposed algorithm outperforms previous approaches for improving the system capacity.

articleTitle: A novel disturbance observer for attitude control of flexible spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper introduce the high accuracy attitude control method of spacecraft with flexible appendages. It is known that the unwanted vibration modes of flexible appendages will degrade the performance of the flexible spacecraft attitude control system. In this paper, the vibration modes are considered as an `equivalent' disturbance, and a novel nonlinear disturbance observer is designed to estimate this `equivalent' disturbance. A disturbance feed-forward compensate controller (DFCC) is designed based on the nonlinear disturbance observer and the feedback linearization control to improve the performance of attitude control system. The flexible spacecraft is controlled by the actuator locate on the central rigid body. Simulation results investigate that the DFCC designed in this paper improved the performance of the attitude control system.

articleTitle: A framework of stability analysis for multi-agent systems on arbitrary topology graph: A class of nonlinear protocols
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, aiming at consensus analysis at the local multi-agent level and avoiding at the group level, we propose a unified approach for the multi-agent system (MAS) with a class of nonlinear protocols on arbitrary topology graph. This method is unified and different from the existing tools: the Laplacian matrix based method and the Lyapunov's method. It treats the multi-agent system as the composition of many isolated agents and focuses on their input and output relationship. Then, the stability analysis is recursive and independent of the specific topology.

articleTitle: A hybrid energy storage system based on DSP for the ship
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, we built an experimental platform for the hybrid energy storage system for the ship based on DSP28335. The design of bidirectional DC/DC controller is completed. The PI control algorithm to improve the stability of the control system, and two kinds of operating modes of the half bridge bi-directional DC/DC controller for boost and buck, respectively from the angle of voltage and current control for experimental testing. The two working modes are tested respectively from the voltage and current control. Through the research of this system, we can improve the utilization rate and service life of the battery energy, and provide the research foundation for the research of the green energy storage system.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of coupled map car-following model with varying time-delays of drivers
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Based on coupled map car-following model proposed by Konishi, a new kind of coupled map car-following model is proposed and the stabilization issue of new coupled map car-following model under the impact of drivers time-varying delay response time is studied. By using the Lyapunov function theory, the sufficient conditions that the existence of state feedback controller for the closed-loop car-following model is stable is given, which indicates that the phenomenon of traffic congestion can be effectively suppressed, the controller can be obtained by solving the LMIs. Finally, through some simulation example verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of method.

articleTitle: NN-based adaptive stabilization for a class of stochastic nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The output tracking problem is considered for a class of stochastic nonlinear systems with unknown control coefficients in this paper. By combining the radial basis function neural network (RBF NN) approximation method with backstepping technique, an adaptive state-feedback controller is successfully constructed to guarantee the solution process to be bounded in probability. In addition, the tracking error signal is 4th-moment semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded, which can also be regulated into a small neighborhood of the origin in probability. Finally, a simulation example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: On delay-dependent stability for linear systems with interval time-varying delays
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this note, the problem of stability for linear systems with interval time-varying delays is investigated. New Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals (LKFs) are constructed which contain more information of delay and some triple-integral terms. By combining Jensen's integral inequality with delay decomposition technique and convex combination approach, the upper bound of the derivative of the Lyapunov functional can be estimated more tightly. As a result, some novel less conservative stability criteria are formulated in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Numerical examples authenticate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Distributed reliable L2 — L∞ state estimation for discrete-time delayed neural networks with missing measurements
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the distributed L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> - L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> state estimation for discrete-time delayed neural networks with missing measurements and sensor failures. The model of neural networks is constructed by the combination with nonlinear functions and state space expressions. Time-varying delays are assumed to have the lower bounds and the upper bounds, and the missing measurements and the sensor failures are described by a stochastic Bernoulli distributed variable and uncertainties, respectively. By using a distributed network, Kronecker product, linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) technology and the solving optimization problems, a sufficient condition is derived to ensure that the filtering error system is stochastically asymptotically stable and achieves the optimal L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> - L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> performance. Finally, a simulation example is given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Stochastic distributed consensus with quantized data and input noise
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper studies the problem of distributed average consensus with input noise and the quantized data. We assume the network, which is expressed by a first-order difference equation. We suppose that the topologies of the network are fixed, and noise is added after encoding and furthermore, some conditions are derived to achieve convergence. However, the weight in our approach is forced to satisfy a persistence condition, and assume that the quantization level is bounded, we prove that there is a stochastic final state for each agent to approach. Furthermore, the rate of convergence of the mean consensus and the statistic properties, such as unbiasedness and mean square error are analyzed in detail. Interestingly, the tradeoff between the convergence rate and the mean square error are found, then a numerical study is also illustrated.

articleTitle: Novel adaptive dynamic surface control of nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: A novel adaptive dynamic surface control (DSC) with recursive error surface is proposed for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems in strict-feedback form. The problem of explosion of terms in traditional backstepping design is eliminated by utilizing dynamic surface control. Furthermore, the maximum value of the norm of the ideal weighting vector in neural network (NN) systems is considered as the estimation parameter, such that only one parameter is adjusted regardless of the number of the NN nodes in whole design procedure. In particular, By designing recursive error surface, the tracking error in the preceding step is considered into the next control law so that the design synthesizes the interaction of the tracking error in each subsystem. The problem for DSC being fragile to the perturbation of its own parameters is avoided. Via constructing new Lyapunov function, the semi-global stability of the close-loop system is proved. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the control scheme.

articleTitle: Reheated steam temperature control based on the γ incremental SGPC-PID
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: With the changing of power supply pattern, almost all the large capacity thermal power units are used to depth peak load cycling, which causes reheated steam temperature fluctuated big and frequently. And in such a situation, the thermal power units can't work very safely and efficiently. In this paper the γ incremental SGPC-PID cascade control scheme is proposed, which solved the fluctuating problem of reheated steam temperature. The GPC is firstly introduced to overcome the reheated steam temperature's fluctuating problem, and then the stair like control scheme and γ factor are introduced to avoid the matrix inversion and simplify the parameter adjustment of GPC. The γ incremental SGPC-PID cascade control algorithm fully develops the PID's anti-interference ability and the SGPC's strong adaptability to large inertia and large time delay. Simulation results show that with better robustness and anti-disturbance performance, this control scheme not only improves the dynamic and static performance of reheated steam temperature, but also it has the advantage of computation simple and parameter adjust easily.

articleTitle: The impact of hybrid quarantine strategies and delay factor on viral prevalence in computer networks
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Recently, the quarantine approach, which has been applied to infectious disease control, is widely regarded as an effective measure to suppress viral spread in computer networks. Hence, in order to prevent the spread of computer virus in network, and consider the latent period of a latent computer, a new delayed epidemic model of computer virus with hybrid quarantine strategies is presented. By regarding the delay as bifurcating parameter and analyzing the associated characteristic equation, the dynamical behaviors, including local asymptotical stability in which the virus spreading can be controlled, and furthermore, local Hopf bifurcation occurs in the system, which implies computer virus is out of control, are investigated. By applying the normal form and center manifold theorem, the direction of Hopf bifurcation and the stability of bifurcating periodic solutions are also determined. Some numerical simulations are provided to support our theoretical results which also imply that hybrid quarantine strategies can inhibit viral spread effectively, and make the model be asymptotically stable.

articleTitle: On delay-range-dependent stability for linear systems with time-varying delays
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This note concerns with the stability problem of linear systems with time-varying delay in a given range. A modified augmented Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF) is constructed where the information on the lower, upper bounds of the delay is fully exploited. By some ingenious techniques and different tackle from the literature, the derivative of the LKF is enlarged as an affine function on the delay. According to the property of an affine function, new delay-range-dependent criteria with less conservatism are derived in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Numerical examples authenticate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Boundary analysis in block schemes for control of some multi-level quantum systems
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Two-photon absorption (TPA) is an important quantum process in the light-matter interaction. When more than one TPA pathway exists in a quantum system, it is necessary to utilize the interference of these pathways to increase the sum TPA amplitude. A simple block scheme (Phys. Rev. A 2013, 88, 053427) is proposed to maximize the constructive interference of two TPA pathways in a four-level diamond-configuration quantum system. It can also be expanded to control multiple TPA pathways (Chin. J. Chem. Phys. 2015, 28, 426). The spectral boundaries in the scheme is related to the energy structure of the system. This work tries to give an analysis of the boundaries for general four-level and five-level quantum systems, which have two and three TPA pathways, respectively. How the boundaries and thus the number of blocks change with the energy structure will be explored.

articleTitle: Observer-based output feedback control for T-S fuzzy time-delay systems
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This study is concerned with the problem of observer-based output feedback control for T-S fuzzy systems with time-delay under imperfect premise matching. The objective is to design an observer-based controller such that the closed-loop control system is asymptotically stable. The proposed fuzzy controller and fuzzy observer do not need to share the same premise membership functions and number of rules with T-S fuzzy systems, which makes the controller and observer design more flexible. Using a recently developed integral inequality, a delay-dependent method for the controller and observer design is provided. With the help of some advanced matrix inequalities, the proposed conditions are presented in the form of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). An illustrative example is given to show the effectiveness of the present result.

articleTitle: Boundary control based on an infinite dimensional system of a marine riser with constraint
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, the constrained problem of the joint angles for a flexible marine riser is investigated. The riser system is described by partial differential equations (PDEs) - ordinary differential equations (ODEs), which avoid the spillover effect. Boundary control based on the integral-barrier Lyapunov function (IBLF) is achieved by three actuators equipped at the top boundary of the riser. Under the time-varying disturbances, the designed control can suppress vibration of the riser and ensure joint angles in the constrained range. The stability is proved under the designed control laws. Numerical simulations are given to illustrate the effectiveness of the designed control laws.

articleTitle: Study of fuel film parameter identification in gasoline engine transient conditions based on weighted recursive instrumental variable method
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: It is very important for transient air-fuel ratio control to obtain the fuel film dynamic parameters precisely. The fuel film identification equation based on the inlet fuel film dynamic model is built under the consideration of random errors. In order to eliminate the effect of random errors on the fuel film parameter estimation, instrumental variable (IV) method is put forward. At the same time, considering that each set of measurement data have different confidence coefficient in terms of parameters estimation, the weighted term is introduced to the instrumental variable equation. An engine model is set up using EN-DYNA. Parameter identification applying the proposed algorithm, least squares and Markov recursive least squares are conducted respectively at 1500–3000r/min and the throttle opening from 10%–80%. The identification results are compared and analyzed with the calibration value. The results show that maximum deviation of X and τ applying the weighted recursive instrumental variable method are 1.58% and 4.5% respectively. However, the maximum deviation of X and τ are 2.37% and 6.18% in Markov recursive least squares method meanwhile the value are 4.08% and 9.16% in least squres method.

articleTitle: Partial blurred object segmentation for non-uniform motion degraded images
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Many computer vision tasks, such as video surveillance, motion analysis and object recognition, need accurate object segmentation results. Nevertheless, good segmentation is difficult to be obtained by most state-of-the-art algorithms in non-uniform degraded images. In this paper, we present an efficient object segmentation method to deal with such problem. First, superpixel-based pairwise fuzzy connectedness and motion orientation are combined as a compounded feature for improving the robustness of segmentation. Second, a superpixel-based quick searching strategy is introduced for background-searching-based object segmentation via the proposed compounded features. We compare the proposed method with state-of-the-art object segmentation algorithms on several open datasets [25][26] quantitatively and qualitatively. The experiments show that our results achieve a good performance in normal images. In addition, our proposed method outperforms the other algorithms on the complex non-uniform motion degraded images obviously.

articleTitle: Short-term power load forecasting based on improved T-S fuzzy-neural network
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: At present, in terms of the influences of temperature and holidays on the power load, an improved T-S fuzzy-neural network is proposed to forecast the short-term power load. Considering the learning rate and smoothing factor should be adjusted dynamically for the higher performance of T-S fuzzy-neural network, the two optimal parameters must be found automatically when the parameters are changed. Thus a T-S fuzzy-neural network based on the Particle Swarm Optimization(PSO) to adjust parameters dynamically is proposed. Firstly, the stable intervals of the parameters must be found, so that parameters can be adjusted dynamically in the intervals. Secondly, the PSO is introduced to find the optimal parameters, therefore the system can converge to a stable state rapidly, and achieve an optimal control precision. Finally, combining with data of power load, temperature and holidays provided by the UNITE(the European Network of Excellence on Intelligent Technologies for Smart Adaptive Systems)web, and the MATLAB simulation results analysis, the improved T-S network has been proved a higher control precision in power load forecasting.

articleTitle: An improved word segmentation algorithm for lip-reading
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: An improved word segmentation algorithm is proposed, which is used to find out the section that represents the pronunciation part from the video frame sequence in the computer lip-reading system. In the computer lip-reading system, after extracting the lip features, the standard deviation of the lip features is calculated. Then the paper proposes the word segmentation method based on the standard deviation and the results show that this method can only be used to determine the approximate pronunciation section and that cannot accurately determine the location of the beginning and the ending of the pronunciation position. So an improved method is presented that the location of the beginning and the ending of the pronunciation section is determined according to the distribution of the gradient of the standard deviation. The results show that the improved method can greatly improves the accuracy of locating of the beginning and the ending of the pronunciation section.

articleTitle: The effect of inhibitory feedback on temporal regularity in neural networks
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The regularity of the spiking activity is closely related to the neural encoding and transmission of neural information. However, it is largely unknown how the inhibitory feedback, as a common interaction existed in cortex, contributes to the precise transmission of neural information. In order to explore the answer to this question, we construct a feed-forward network (FFN) model with lateral inhibitory circuits and study the effect of inhibitory feedback on the temporal regularity of spiking activities. Besides, we discuss the spike-time regularity of pure FFN model without feedback for selecting typical dynamic states of neural network. Results show that the inhibitory feedback with adaptive strength enhance the regularity of spike-time in typical states. It indicates that the spike-time regularity observed in the experiment is resulted by the interaction between feed-forward and inhibitory feedback.

articleTitle: Distributed optimization strategy for multi-region power scheduling based on alternating direction method of multipliers
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The large-scale and frequent cross-regional electricity allocations bring about the critical need to coordinate multi-region power scheduling. It is recognized that each sub-systems' taking charge of own scheduling makes the ideal centralized optimization method infeasible. In this paper, a distributed optimization strategy based on alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is put forward to solve this problem. The strategy can achieve optimal solution of global power system as the ideal centralized optimization method does, by adding steps of information exchange and iterations of decision variables to subsystems' independent scheduling. The distributed bid cost minimization model with a price-wise constant bidding curve is built to describe the multi-region scheduling problem as precisely as possible. To suit the distributed model, the standard ADMM is improved, by expanding the size of sub-systems, adding inequality constraints, and considering the complex coupling relationship between sub-systems. This coordinating strategy uses the framework of augmented Lagrangian to decompose the scheduling problem into a distributed scheduling model for regional power grid, achieving global optimal solution by updating decision variables of each sub-system and Lagrange multipliers with mapping of sub-system information. Simulations on IEEE 30 system are conducted to show the computational performance and solution quality of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A dynamical compliant grasping strategy for dexterous robotic hands with cushioning mechanism
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamical compliant grasping problem for a class of dexterous robotic hands. In particular, a novel bio-inspired cushioning mechanism is introduced, which can guarantee the compliant achievement of grasping the moving objects. With visual information of the moving objects, the grasping strategy can be implemented for dexterous robotic hands with two specific space regions at different stages. Compared with traditional grasping methods, significant advantages can be obtained such as grasping feasibility, stability and flexibility. Finally, the experimental example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of our obtained theoretical results.

articleTitle: Integrated fault detection and control for 2-D Roesser systems
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of integrated fault detection and control for two-dimensional (2-D) Roesser systems. A fault detection detector/controller is designed to detect faults in low-frequency domain effectively and satisfy some control specifications simultaneously. By the generalized KYP lemma and bounded real lemma, it is formulated as a multiobjective optimization problem. A two-step algorithm is proposed to solve this nonconvex problem. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is illustrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Adaptive fuzzy tracking control for switched stochastic nonlinear systems with input constraint
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of adaptive fuzzy tracking control for a class of uncertain strict-feedback stochastic nonlinear systems with input constraint under arbitrary switchings. The input constraint is approximated by a smooth function, and fuzzy logic systems are employed to identify the unknown nonlinear functions. On the basis of the backstepping technique and the common Lyapunov function method, a new adaptive fuzzy tracking control scheme is proposed, which ensures semi-globally uniformly ultimately boundedness in probability of all signals in the closed-loop systems and enables the reference signal to be tracked with bounded error. Finally, a numerical example is given to show the effectiveness of the developed control scheme.

articleTitle: Event-triggered network-based control of discrete-time singular systems
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the problem of event-triggered control for a networked discrete-time singular system. A novel event-triggered networked control scheme is proposed to save the limited network communication bandwidth. By using a delay system approach, a unified model of event-triggered control system is established. A new criterion is proposed in terms of strict linear matrix inequality (LMI) by using Lyapunov functional method, which guarantees the admissibility of the discrete-time networked singular system without resorting to decomposing the system matrices. A state feedback controller is then designed based on this criterion. Finally, a numerical example is provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Simulation design of rolling tube machine mandrel support device hydraulic system
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Compared the mechanical adjustment with hydraulic position closed-loop adjustment, the structure of mandrel supporting device of rolling tube machine is analyzed in this paper, then the AMESim software is applied to model the position closed-loop control hydraulic system dynamics based on its structure parameters, where the simulation results play an important role in designing the hydraulic control system. Moreover, simulation results and experimental data also show that the method proposed in this paper is very effective. After that, the two-dimensional simulation environment is constructed and simulated based on AMESim, which can display the process of each system device before the system design, providing the reference for the hydraulic machine and equipment design.

articleTitle: Modeling and vibration control of flexible wings with output constraint
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, we present modeling and vibration control with boundary output constraint. By using the Hamilton's principle, the dynamics of the flexible wings are represented by partial differential equations (PDEs) and several ordinary differential equations (ODEs). Based on the Lyapunov's direct method, model-based barrier control is developed to control the vibrations of the flexible wings under the boundary output constraint. To achieve the constraint violation, a novel barrier Lyapunov function is employed for the control design and stability analysis. The vibration suppress is well achieved without violation of constraint.

articleTitle: The design of automatic frequency and load modulation of marine PMS based on ControlLogix
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: According to the development situation of shipping power system technology and all electric propulsion ships, the application of marine power management system has become the inevitable trend of the development of the ship in the future. Ship power station is playing a vital part in providing electric power for navigation. The stability of the ship power system certainly influences the function of frequency and load modulation. As an important part, the marine power management system (PMS) is efficiently used in the ship power station. So when ships face extreme conditions with good function of frequency and load modulation, PMS can effectively reduce the fluctuations caused by thrusters while having heavy torque changes. Meanwhile, this paper come up with a new control system that is automatic frequency and load modulation of marine PMS based on ControlLogix, to obviously reduce the oscillation of power and frequency.

articleTitle: Multivariate order recurrence network for analyzing cross-correlation of the wind field and the gas concentration field
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Uncovering the cross-correlation between wind signals and gas concentration signals is a challenging problem of significant importance. We first measure six groups of multivariate signals which contain wind speed time series, wind direction time series and gas concentration time series. Then, the order patterns analysis is employed to construct recurrence matrices and we can infer multivariate recurrence networks from these experimental data. Next, we extract the cross-clustering coefficient and the cross-transitivity to quantitatively assess the derived networks. The results suggest that the cross-clustering coefficient can accurately reflect the coupling relationship between the wind signals and the gas concentration signals. Moreover, the cross-transitivity is very sensitive to the locations of sensors with different distances to the gas leakage source. In this regard, bridging the multivariate signals analysis and complex networks can be a fascinating method for coupling analysis of different types of flow fields.

articleTitle: Functional connectivity estimation with general linear model
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Inferring neuron network construction, the ideal situation is to explore the relationship between synaptic and functional connection. In this paper, we apply the general linear model(GLM) to construct a two coupled neuron functional network, then based on neuron spiking point process and maximum likelihood estimation we can estimate the functional connectivity. By using fixed and unfixed method, we find that general linear model can perfectly infer functional connectivity meanwhile make good fit with the original input-output data. Moreover, through the comparison of the two methods we know the unfixed way is better and these results can be further used for large-scale network construction and connectivity analysis.

articleTitle: Bus signal priority method assessment based on multiple attribute group decision
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This thesis puts forward a bus signal priority assessment index system, which including bus traffic efficiency, intersection traffic efficiency, implementation difficulty factors of methods and so on. Because there are some missing, uncertain or fuzzy indices, and relevance between indices. And decision-makers would have their subjective preferences. The thesis then puts forward a bus signal priority assessment method based on uncertain multiple attribute group decision. At the last part, the thesis takes Guangzhou Tianhe Road and Tiyudong Road intersection as an example to assess bus signal priority method, including no priority, all priority and general fuzzy control priority, and verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Kinematics and dynamics modelling of all terrain articulated tracked vehicles
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper presents an extended kinematics and dynamics of the articulated tracked vehicles (ATV) used in many applications. The velocity of the front and the rear vehicle are firstly analysed and the kinematics of ATV is built, according to which the steer radius and the track velocity can be obtained. Then we analyse the force and moment acting on the ATV running on the firm ground and the soft ground, respectively. And a unified dynamics is established in a matrix form. To show the motion performance of the ATV, simulations are performed and the results are further presented.

articleTitle: Causality analysis during shared intentionality
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Causal interaction between different brain regions has received wide attention recently. Granger causality (GC) is one of the most popular methods to explore causality relationship between different brain regions. New causality (NC) proposed by Hu et. al was shown to be better reveal true causality than GC. In this paper based on scalp EEGs from 6 groups subjects we apply GC and NC methods to study shared intentionality which is an important mental process in cognitive neuroscience and psychology. We are interested in nine regions: F3 (left area of the frontal cortex), Fz (central area of the frontal cortex), F4 (right area of the frontal cortex), C3 (left area of the central cortex), Cz (central area of the central cortex), C4 (right area of the central cortex), P3 (left area of the parietal cortex), Pz (central area of the parietal cortex), P4 (right area of the parietal cortex) which are considered to be optimal locations for observing whether the scalp EEGs can yield information about the timing of episodically synchronized brain activity in higher cognitive function. Our findings show that i) there exists obvious stronger causal influence from F3/Fz/F4/Cz/C4/P3/Pz/P4 to C3 in 8 ~ 13Hz rhythm than that from C3 to F3/Fz/F4/Cz/C4/P3/Pz/P4 for three states (eyes open+finger movement, eyes wandering+finger movement, and eyes close+finger movement) during shared intentionality. ii) NC method can better reveal real causal influence in 8 ~ 13Hz rhythm than GC method during three states.

articleTitle: Maximum likelihood least squares iterative identification algorithm for hammerstein output error moving average systems
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper studies the parameter estimation problem of Hammerstein output error moving average (OEMA) systems. According to the maximum likelihood principle and iterative identification technique, a maximum likelihood least squares iterative identification (ML-LSI) algorithm is proposed. A numerical example is provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Improved delay-range-dependent stability for linear systems with time-varying delays based on affine function
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this brief, the problem of stability for linear systems with interval time-varying delays is investigated. A type of new augmented Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKFs) are constructed where more information of delay and some triple-integral terms are included. By our lemmas and others bounded techniques, the upper bound of derivative of the proposed LKFs can be expressed as an affine function with respect to the delay. Based on property of the affine function, improved delay-range dependent stability criteria with less conservative are derived in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Numerical examples authenticate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An improved load-shedding model based on power flow tracing
publicationTitle: 2016 12th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
